chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, who washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام? He said: That was Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.

He said: It was as though I considered that a grave matter from what he said, so he said: It is as though you felt constrained by what I informed you of? I said: Indeed that was so, may I be made your ransom.
So he said: Do not be constrained, for she is a Ṣiddīqah; none but a Ṣiddīq would wash her. Do you not know that Maryam عليها السلام was washed by none but ʿĪsā عليه السلام?

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام
key_terms.صِدِّيقٌ: a supremely truthful and veracious man
key_terms.صِدِّيقَةٌ: a supremely truthful and veracious woman
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Lady Fāṭimah عليها السلام, daughter of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Mary, mother of ʿĪsā عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Who washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and does this hadith show that a husband may wash his wife after death?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام after her death. When the narrator found this difficult, Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explained that she was a Ṣiddīqah and that only a Ṣiddīq would wash her, citing Maryam عليها السلام and ʿĪsā عليه السلام as a precedent. It is used in the context of the permissibility of a husband and wife washing one another after death.
